subject: Mathematics
source: Phase F · FEAT-PF1 — author-original scaffold rows for the highest-volume Edexcel Y10 maths spec points (1MA1).

sentenceFrames: First, I will expand the bracket: ______ × ______ + ______ × ______.
Then, I will collect the x-terms on one side: ______.
Finally, I will divide both sides by ______ to get x = ______.

wordBank.definition: a statement that two expressions are equal, with an equals sign
move terms across the equals sign by doing the opposite operation
get the unknown letter on its own on one side

stepLadder: Move all the x-terms to one side using +/−.
Move all the numbers to the other side using +/−.
Divide both sides by the coefficient of x.
Check by substituting your answer back into the original equation.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting to apply the same operation to both sides.
Sign errors when moving a negative term across the equals sign.
Dividing only one side by the coefficient at the end.
rows.visualAidHint: Drawing balance scales with the equation either side reminds pupils that whatever you do to one side you must do to the other.

sentenceFrames: I'm looking for two numbers that multiply to ______ and add to ______.
So x² + bx + c factorises as (x + ______)(x + ______).
Setting each bracket equal to zero, x = ______ or x = ______.

wordBank.definition: rewrite as a product of two brackets
an equation of the form ax² + bx + c = 0
a value of x that makes the equation equal zero

stepLadder: Make sure the equation equals zero (move all terms to one side if needed).
Identify b (the coefficient of x) and c (the constant term).
Find two numbers that multiply to give c and add to give b.
Write the factors as (x + p)(x + q) = 0.
Set each bracket equal to zero and solve for x.
Check both solutions by substituting back into the original equation.
commonPitfalls: Forgetting to set the equation to zero before factorising.
Sign errors when c is negative (one of the factors must be negative).
rows.visualAidHint: A factor pair table for c, with the sum of each pair, makes the search systematic.

sentenceFrames: The multiplier for ______ % per year is 1 + ______ /100 = ______.
The investment is worth £______ to the nearest penny.

wordBank.definition: interest earned on the original amount AND on previously earned interest
the number you multiply by each year (e.g. 1.024 for 2.4%)

stepLadder: Convert the percentage rate to a decimal (e.g. 2.4% → 0.024).
Raise the multiplier to the power of the number of years.
commonPitfalls: Using simple interest by mistake (multiplying the interest by the number of years).
Forgetting to round to 2 decimal places for money.
